packageRules.description: Anything that is not a major arrives, passes the checks and merges itself without ever opening a pull request. If the checks fail, Renovate raises one instead, so a failure is the only thing that asks for attention. What is left to look at is only what needed deciding.

The build toolchain is the exception, and reviewed by hand however small the version bump looks. Everything else is judged by CI; this is what CI is built out of, so a passing run is weaker evidence than usual - a compiler that changed its output validates itself. Kotlin and AGP also call changes minor that are nothing of the sort.
Kotlin, its compiler plugins and KSP are released against each other. Updating one without the others is how a build stops compiling for reasons that look unrelated.
The Compose BOM decides the version of everything under androidx.compose, so they move together whether or not Renovate is told.
Room's runtime, compiler and testing artefacts share a version and will not work if they drift apart.
The Android Gradle plugin decides which SDK, which Gradle and which Java the build needs, so it travels alone.
One pull request a week for the workflows rather than one per action.
Rust patch and minor updates are rarely interesting on their own.
Same for the web application's own dependencies.
A floating tag is already whatever it is; a pull request saying so tells nobody anything.
A major version is a decision rather than an update, so it arrives on its own and says so.
